stock.counterargument: Growth decelerated against the previous quarter, so the trend in the numbers is already turning.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below -1.9%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $47.64 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 127 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 127 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-04.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-11-07) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Big Tech’s big AI buildout will not end until someone stops it
stories.excerpt: After four of the biggest competitors in the AI race held quarterly earnings calls late last month, two things are clear: Big Tech is not done spending record amounts on the AI data center buildout, and the AI data center buildout is not any closer to yielding its promised returns. A third thing is…
stories.lead:
A third thing is also starting to become clear — Big Tech will not be slowing down, at least not on its own.

Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta told investors they’re planning to spend at least $720 billion on CapEx this year alone. Most of that will go toward AI infrastructure. That’s on top of at least $1 trillion in spending commitments that have been arranged for the coming years.

stories.title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation
stories.excerpt: Five of France's unions have joined a wave of strikes and protests in a national day of action.
stories.lead:
Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators are expected to take part in marches across France as five unions join strikes and protests in a national day of action.

The protests began in September with high school students complaining about poor conditions and resources in education, but have spread to include the so-called "yellow-vest" movement and workers.

Authorities expect 500,000 to 700,000 demonstrators to join marches, with tens of thousands more in Paris alone, in a day billed by one union leader as "a great day of convergence".

stories.title: Trump's arch is on the verge of federal approval. But a judge could block construction
stories.excerpt: A federal panel will meet to consider the arch for final approval on Thursday, and the government said it may begin construction later that same day. Critics hope a judge will intervene last-minute.
stories.lead:
This could be a make-or-break week for President Trump's triumphal arch.

For months, the Trump administration has barreled toward his dream of building a 250-foot arch in Washington, D.C.: rubber-stamping and side-stepping various federal reviews, cutting out Congress and announcing imminent construction despite a lack of final approval and an ongoing legal battle.

In May, the entirely Trump-appointed Commission for Fine Arts approved the arch's design — still incomplete at the time. In September, a federal council packed with Trump allies abruptly terminated a historic preservation review that participants had already criticized as rushed.

stories.title: Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty
stories.excerpt: Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo says he is retiring from international football.
stories.lead:
The 41-year-old forward has scored 146 goals and won 234 caps for his country - both world records - since making his debut in 2003.

His retirement comes after he walked out of the Portugal camp in September after being told he would not start the Nations League match against Denmark, resulting in a £215 fine from the Portuguese Football Federation (PFF).

stories.lead:
Newsflash: The Bank of England has raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years, as policymakers try to fight rising inflation.

Its monetary policy committee has voted to raise Bank rate from 3.75% to 4%, the first rise since August 2023.
